before_times: How many dogs, and how big each one is
Has any dog ever bitten or snapped at a person? (a yes sends the request to the owner first)
The yard: front, back or both; fenced or not; under or over a quarter acre
How long since the yard was last cleaned: a week, a month, or a season or more (a long time is priced from photos)
How often: every week, twice a week, every 2 weeks, or just once
How the tech gets in: an open gate, a latch, or a gate code
after_time: Will the dogs be inside, or behind a second gate, on the service day?
Where the waste goes: taken away by the tech, or into the customer's own bin
Spots to skip: garden beds, buried lines, an invisible fence
Which side of the house the gate is on, and where to park
secure_page_only: The gate, door or alarm code, and where a key is kept
An emergency contact, to call if a dog is out and the customer can't be reached
The landlord's or owner's OK, for a rented or shared yard
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult (18 or older) who lives at the address or owns the yard. A renter of a shared yard needs the owner's OK. Nobody under 18 books.

stop: a dog that is hurt, very sick, struggling to breathe or ate something toxic, right now
a dog loose in the yard that attacks
a dog that got out of the yard and is lost right now
needles, broken glass, a dead animal, sewage or chemicals in the yard
safety_and_stop_words.go_on: No, for an emergency now, or for a hazard reported when booking. Yes, after the owner's OK, for a dog that has bitten. Yes for a hazard found at a visit: the rest of the yard is cleaned.
stop_action: A dog hurt, very sick or poisoned now: Rosie can't judge how sick a pet is. It says to call the vet, or the nearest 24-hour emergency vet, now. No booking until the dog is safe.
A person bitten and hurt: call 911 first.
A dog loose in the yard that attacks: the tech doesn't go in. The customer is told, and the visit waits until the dog is inside. The owner decides any fee.
A lost dog right now: Rosie gives the business's number to call, and tells the owner at once.

Needles, broken glass, a dead animal, sewage or chemicals: reported when booking, it's other work and isn't booked. Found at a visit, the tech leaves that spot alone, sends a photo note, and cleans the rest. Rosie names the kind of company to call, like animal control or a hazard cleanup company, never one by name.

prep: Put the dogs inside or behind a second gate
Leave the gate open, latched or on its code
Move hoses, toys and bowls off the lawn
Put the gate code on the secure page, never in a text

skills: First big cleanups of heavy yards
Yards with nervous or protective dogs
Video yard checks with a written plan (the planning desk)
staff.licenses_or_certificates: None per person unless the city's form says so.
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs a dog with a bite history, every fee and every refund. The office manager may OK prices over the limit; the owner's answer wins.
staff.ratio: One tech at each yard. Two techs for a first big cleanup of a large yard.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult (18 or older) who lives at the address or owns the yard. A renter of a shared yard needs the owner's OK. Nobody under 18 books.
children_and_age.minors_texts: Nobody under 18 books. A teen at home isn't the booking's adult.

visit.check_in: Nobody home, no code: the tech opens the gate as set on the secure page, texts IN, and texts DONE with the yard report and a photo. When the customer is home, the code at the gate works as usual. A video yard check: the customer joins by video, and the planner reads the code out at the start.
visit.done: DONE with the yard report and a photo of the clean yard and the latched gate.
visit.changes_at_visit: A bigger yard or more dogs than booked: the tech cleans what was booked and texts a note. A higher price needs the customer's yes first, and is paid with the visit (the card at DONE, or the bill).

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Usually none: most places license neither pet waste removal nor yard cleanup. Some cities or counties ask for a business license, and some ask for a permit to haul waste away for pay. The state's or city's form says which.
license.who: The business. A waste hauling permit, where one is needed, is held by the business, not by each tech.
license.ask: The business registration or local business license number, where the form asks for one. A waste hauling permit, where the form asks for it.
license.insurance: General liability insurance is shown as given by the business, not checked by Rosie.
license.background: Only where the rules require them, or as the business's own word. Techs work alone in a customer's yard, so a business check of its own is common.

never_in_a_text: Gate, door, garage and alarm codes
A dog's health conditions and medicines
